text: We evaluate the baseline agent and the agent with the new retrieval tool on the same 120 tasks from our internal benchmark. Each configuration is run 3 times per task. The new tool variant is allowed up to 3 retries per task and we keep the best run. Runs that time out are excluded from the analysis. Outputs are graded by a GPT-4-class judge that sees the full transcript, including the system prompt. We report the success rate over all runs and test significance with a two-proportion z-test. The baseline currently solves about 41% of tasks. We ran the baseline first, then the variant the following week.

Both agents were run on the same 200 tasks, 5 attempts per task each, interleaved in random order on the same pinned model snapshot within a single day. The two system prompts are identical except for the tool description being tested. Failures, timeouts and unparseable outputs are scored as failures for both agents. A judge model graded anonymized transcripts with the condition labels removed. Our pre-registered primary metric is task success; significance is assessed with a paired t-test on per-task success rates. Baseline success is 55%; we consider a 5-point gain meaningful.
We compare two prompts on 50 questions.
Correctness is checked by unit tests, so no model judge is involved. Both agents attempt each of the 164 problems once.
Agent A was evaluated on the 2024 split (300 tasks) and agent B on the 2025 split (300 different tasks), one run each.
We tracked accuracy, pass@1, pass@5, average steps and cost, and report the metrics on which the new agent improved. 80 tasks, 3 seeds per task.
Responses that could not be parsed into the required JSON format were dropped before scoring. Both agents ran on the same 90 tasks.
Unparseable responses count as incorrect for both systems.
The improved agent was given a budget of 50 tool calls per task versus 20 for the baseline.
Baseline runs were collected in March on gpt-x-0301; the new agent was evaluated in May after the provider's model update.
The new system prompt adds the planning module description and also tells the model to 'think carefully and double-check your work', which the old prompt did not include.
We compute 95% confidence intervals with a bootstrap that resamples tasks, on 250 shared tasks with 4 runs each per agent.
With 40 tasks x 10 runs we have 400 samples per condition, and a chi-squared test on the pooled pass counts gives p = 0.01.
An LLM judge rated each answer on a 1-10 scale; the judge prompt states which system produced the answer so it can account for system-specific formatting.
If an episode crashes or exceeds the 10-minute limit, it is recorded as a failure for whichever agent was running.
Our current agent resolves 31% of issues. We would ship the new scaffold only if it adds at least 4 percentage points.
The new version feels a lot better in our demos and the team is excited to ship it.
Both versions use best-of-5 sampling with the same verifier, on the same 75 tasks, run concurrently against the same API version.
We pre-registered success rate as the single primary metric before running anything.

On 60 shared tasks (3 attempts each), the variant passed 52% vs 45% for the baseline. We excluded 7 tasks where the variant hit a tool error, and graded with a judge that only saw the final answers without any system identifiers.
